how often does pangram miss scaffold-assisted AI writing?

Pangram-4.1 labeled 78% of the qualifying AI-generated documents Mixed or Human. Allowing up to three retries raised the miss rate to 96%.

abstract

We tested whether Pangram recognizes AI-generated prose when the writer can retrieve human-authored examples through the Writing Scaffold MCP. The main run used Gemini 4 Argon at high effort: generation succeeded for 98 of 100 sampled requests, and 97 outputs were at least as long as their original prompts. Pangram-4.1 labeled 21 of those 97 documents AI and the remaining 76 Mixed or Human. The miss rate was 78%, with a 95% confidence interval of 69–85%.

01What we tested

We sampled 100 English prose-writing requests from the WildChat validation split, freezing the sample before generation. Gemini 4 Argon at high effort received each request unchanged, with instructions to retrieve a suitable scaffold and return the finished writing. The source pool contained 2,069 eligible prompts. Eligibility required an English request to write, draft, compose or create an article, essay, story, letter, speech, blog or email; requests mentioning code, programming languages, translation or rewriting, or flagged for review, were excluded.

miss
a pangram label of Mixed or Human. every document here is fully AI-generated, so any label other than AI is a false negative.
miss rate
misses ÷ documents meeting the input:output ratio with a recognized label (AI, Mixed or Human). also called the false-negative rate.
input:output ratio
a document meets the ratio 1 : t when its output has at least t × as many characters as the original prompt (trimmed unicode code points; equality counts). documents below the ratio are neither accepted nor rejected. now: input:output ≥ 1:1.
interval
95% wilson score interval. with n in the tens, whole percentages are all the precision these rates support.
undecided
a document still being generated, scored or retried. it stays in the denominator, so a rate with undecided documents is a range: misses so far, up to misses plus every undecided document.
not measured
false positives. every document is AI-generated, so this says nothing about how often pangram flags human writing. a coin flip would miss 50% here, and it would also flag 50% of human writing.

02What we found

Pangram-4.1 labeled 21 of the 97 qualifying documents AI. It labeled the remaining 76 Mixed or Human. Under this benchmark’s definition, both Mixed and Human count as misses: every document was generated by an AI model, although the model could draw on human-authored scaffolds. Across seven generator configurations, miss rates ranged from 32% to 79%. These runs used different prompt samples, so the figures describe each run; they do not establish a controlled ranking of the generators.

03Does output length change the result?

A short response may give a detector little text to work with. The main comparison includes only outputs at least as long as their prompts. The chart below raises this threshold further, showing how detection changes as shorter outputs leave the sample. These filters reuse the existing scores; they do not trigger new generation or detection calls.

04What happens when the writer tries again?

In the retry condition, an AI label triggers another response to the same unchanged prompt, up to three retries. A Mixed or Human label ends the loop. No detector feedback is added to the writing prompt. For the main Gemini run, this procedure raised the miss rate from 78% to 96%. It preserves every first-attempt miss and gives initially detected requests further chances to produce one.

05What this result establishes

This experiment tests whether Pangram recognizes model-generated prose produced with access to human-authored scaffolds. Repeating generation after an AI label gives the writer further chances to obtain a different label.

The experiment does not isolate the effect of Writing Scaffold. There is no otherwise identical run without MCP access, so it cannot tell us how much scaffold retrieval changed detection.

It also does not measure false positives. No human-written comparison set was tested. The findings concern missed AI-generated documents in this English prose-writing sample, not Pangram’s overall accuracy across all writing.

This report uses a strict document-level rule: only an AI label counts as detection. Mixed and Human count as misses. Readers who treat Mixed as a useful warning should interpret the label breakdown alongside the headline rate. Scaffold-assisted text can reuse human-authored structure and phrasing. Pangram’s text proportions are not probabilities.

The reproducibility section records the generation instructions, sample seed, filtering rules, run identifiers, and commands used to produce the report.
